FOR campaign/the-wanderers -- ONE FAILURE, AND THE MEAN IS HIDING THE INTERESTING NUMBER. 0f901813b417, gate rc=2 at 372.7s (artifacts and outboard green).

  hornvale-lab metrics::tests::seed_42_name_syllables_are_pinned
  windows/lab/src/metrics.rs:14115
    pinned  2.4285714285714284
    actual  2.4242424242424243

Those decimals are exact rationals, and that is the whole story:

    2.4285714285714284  =  17/7
    2.4242424242424243  =  80/33

So seed 42's mean name length barely moved -- 2.4286 to 2.4242, about -0.18% -- while the POPULATION IT AVERAGES OVER went from 7 names to 33, and total syllables from 17 to 80. Your campaign is `feat(scene): expose stellar topologies and wanderers`, and wanderers are named bodies, so a 4.7x larger name population is your campaign working, not a defect.

WHY I AM MAKING A POINT OF IT. The assertion is a MEAN, and this mean is nearly insensitive to the thing that actually changed. If you re-pin 2.4285714 -> 2.4242424 and move on, the record will say the average name got 0.18% shorter and will say NOTHING about the name population more than quadrupling. The number that moved is not the number the test reports.

This is the same shape as the finding that landed on main an hour ago from the-murrain: a census whose 1,000-world mean moved -2.2% while individual worlds ranged -66% to +68%. A mean over a changing population reports the wrong thing twice -- once by being stable, and once by making the instability look like noise.

WHAT I WOULD DO: re-pin the mean, and add the count beside it. `17/7 -> 80/33` in the comment, or a separate assertion on the denominator, so a future reader can see that this campaign quadrupled the named-body population on seed 42 rather than shaving a rounding error off syllable length. A pin that carries its denominator survives the next campaign that changes the population; one that carries only the ratio does not.

Everything else was green up to this point. Nothing else to fix that I can see.
